# hardware
MBP 2023 with M2 Max & 32GB RAM

# Browser
some of the key features I look for in a browser are:

* [workspaces](https://vivaldi.com/features/workspaces/) and
[tab stacking](https://help.vivaldi.com/desktop/tabs/tab-stacks/)
because I use tons of tabs.
* [keyboard shortcuts](https://help.vivaldi.com/desktop/shortcuts/keyboard-shortcuts/)
to quickly help me switch between all the workspaces
* [Quick Commands](https://help.vivaldi.com/desktop/shortcuts/quick-commands/)
because who got mental space to remember how to update a setting (like keyboard shortscuts)
* [Sync across devices](https://vivaldi.com/blog/tips/desktop-tips/tip-23/): mobile, desktop(s)

And so therefore I use:

* Vivaldi[^vivaldi-grieve] : `brew install --cask vivaldi`
* Opera Air[^opera-air-note]: `brew install --cask opera-air`


[^vivaldi-grieve]: the sync feature only started to work in 2024,
the browser do crash unexpectedly on startup from time to time,
and the RAM management is just okay... although I do use tons of tabs.
The built in [ProtonVPN](https://vivaldi.com/protonvpn/) is kinda cool.
[^opera-air-note]: because I ❤️ mindfulness, the built in
[Aria AI](https://www.opera.com/nb/features/aria) is pretty good,
and it basically have all the features above

# Editor
My weapon of choice is [zed](https://github.com/zed-industries/zed) which
is actually pretty great for [agentic coding](https://zed.dev/agentic) and
lots of flexibility in terms of choosing your own LLM[^zed-note].

[^zed-note]: 50 Zed-hosted prompt per month using the latest Claude model.
But you could also setup [OpenRouter or Ollama](https://zed.dev/docs/ai/configuration#llm-providers)
or even use your [Co-pilot](https://zed.dev/docs/ai/configuration#github-copilot-chat) quota in zed.

```bash
brew install --cask zed # <1>
```
1. official brew formula is [here](https://formulae.brew.sh/cask/zed)

# The Toolchain

* docker: `brew install --cask docker`
    * you will need to follow [this guide here](https://stackoverflow.com/a/43365425)
    * and you do want the cask version because the [official version for Mac is a GUI](https://stackoverflow.com/a/40523608)... i.e. there are no headless version
    * my [docker cheatsheet](https://gist.github.com/ohjho/af86af1c1dfab4979f6d0543000351cd)

* [macmon](https://medium.com/@vladkens/mac-usage-monitor-in-terminal-meet-macmon-3a3391995224):
    * TUI for monitoring resource use on Apple's ARM architecture MacBook
    * like a much better version of `htop`
    * install: `brew update && brew install macmon`

* [Sequel-Ace](https://github.com/Sequel-Ace/Sequel-Ace?tab=readme-ov-file):
    * MySQL management for macOS
    * install: `brew update && brew install --cask sequel-ace`

* [yt-dlp](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp?tab=readme-ov-file#installation)
    * feature-rich CLI audio/video downloader with support for [thousand of sites](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/blob/master/supportedsites.md),
    including YouTube and Soundcloud
    * it's a bit more advanced with the use of
    [format selection](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp?tab=readme-ov-file#format-selection)
    for selecting the right stream but it also uses `ffmpeg` under the hood to
    merge audio and video streams.
    Format selection [examples are available](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp?tab=readme-ov-file#format-selection-examples).
    * install: `pipx install "yt-dlp[default]"`

* [asciinema](https://docs.asciinema.org/getting-started/)
    * create recording of terminal sessions that's easy to share
    * sharing can be done by embedding the asciinema player[^asciinema-note] or
    converting the recording to gif using [`agg`](https://willschenk.com/labnotes/2025/asciinema_for_terminal_recordings/#headline-2)[^agg-note]
    * install: `pipx install asciinema`

[^asciinema-note]: you will need to upload the created recording, and
the [asciinema player](https://docs.asciinema.org/getting-started/#sharing)
is purpose-built for sharing terminal sessions.
[^agg-note]: you will need to install `agg` using `brew install agg`

## coding agents

* [Claude Code]()
    * native install using [bash](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/setup#install-claude-code)
    * setup [API keys](https://platform.claude.com/settings/keys)
* [OpenCode](https://opencode.ai/docs/#initialize)[^note-zen]: `brew install anomalyco/tap/opencode`
* [Ollama](https://ollama.com/settings)[^note-ollama]
    * [run cloud models](https://docs.ollama.com/cloud): `ollama run qwen3.5:397b-cloud`
    * [coding agents](https://docs.ollama.com/quickstart#coding): `ollama launch claude`
    * and it [also works with zed](https://docs.ollama.com/integrations/zed)

[^note-ollama]: lots changed with ollama [since 2024](ollama.qmd), make sure you upgrade it:
```bash
brew upgrade ollama
ollama serve    # need to get the app running before any running any other commands
ollama sigin    # for using ollama cloud, you'll need an account first
```
[^note-zen]: if you don't `/connect`, [zen's](https://opencode.ai/docs/zen#pricing) free models will be used as default

# python environments
As of 2025[^pre-2024-note], I manage both python versions and virtual environments with [uv](using-uv.qmd)

python based CLIs using [`pipx`](https://github.com/pypa/pipx).

[^pre-2024-note]: I use to manage using `pyenv` and the `virtualenvwrapper`,
see [here](https://gist.github.com/ohjho/8e2556d786b132d724b3914728c7c82f)
for an archive of that setup.
